name: Tobati
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the cited page/section in a held full text of the deciding source (the record's held list should point to litreview/sources/; grade field is blank and can be set now that the quote is confirmed in-hand). The deciding source is the fieldworker's own 2002 sketch and, per Glottolog and web search, the only phonological description of Tobati in existence; 'regularly.. penultimate' matches the fixed-dominant (non-strict) penult penultimate stress. Not 'well-sourced' only because the evidence is one sentence in an 18-page sketch with no detail on exceptions or secondary stress; nothing found suggests the classification is wrong. works still to obtain are low-priority long shots (Indonesian syntax report, Cowan's 1950s notes); no open copies located.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark (2002), 'Tobati', in Lynch, Ross & Crowley (eds.), The Oceanic Languages, sec. 1.3 Syllabification and stress, p. 189 (archive.org djvu full text re-read)
sources.quote: Primary stress in Tobati regularly falls on the penultimate syllable.

sources.quote: 1.3 Syllabification and stress. Primary stress in Tobati regularly falls on the penultimate syllable.
sources.note: Single-sentence statement; no exceptions given ('regularly'). Secondary stress not mentioned. Tone not mentioned anywhere in the chapter (pp. 186-203). Weight: the only remark is on p. 187, 'a sonorant in this position following a non-low vowel in a single-syllable word is often accompanied by a final vowel, /o/, implying that there is a greater degree of syllable weight associated with /a/ than with the other vowels' -- about epenthesis in monosyllables, not tied to stress placement.
